title: Bring Back the Aliases
description: Recreate the ll and grep aliases that a cleanup script removed from .bashrc.
scenario: A 'cleanup' script gutted everyone's .bashrc yesterday and the team lost its muscle-memory aliases. Restore the two documented standards to /home/intern/.bashrc: `alias ll='ls -alF'` and `alias grep='grep --color=auto'`. Aliases only exist in interactive shells, so they live in .bashrc — and they must survive sourcing in a non-interactive test too.
symptoms: `ll` answers 'command not found' in new terminals
grep output has no colour highlighting
The team's .bashrc standard defines exactly two aliases: ll and grep
A cleanup script rewrote .bashrc without the alias block

hints.title: Alias syntax
hints.content: `alias name='expansion'` — with the equals sign attached to the name and the expansion quoted. Spaces around = are an error.

hints.title: Where aliases live
hints.content: Aliases are for interactive convenience, so .bashrc is their home. They are NOT inherited by scripts (that's deliberate — scripts need predictable commands).

hints.title: Verify by sourcing
hints.content: Aliases defined in .bashrc apply after the file is sourced. Test with: `bash -c 'source ~/.bashrc; alias ll'`.

acceptance_criteria.description: sourcing .bashrc in a fresh shell defines the ll alias
